answer: A delta in stake-weighted reputation makes Sybil creation costly: each agent must lock a refundable bond that grows with the number of identities it controls, so a whisper campaign of cheap clones cannot outvote honest participants. New identities start with velvet-gloved limits — tiny transaction caps that rise only after consistent, attested work over time — so an attacker must sustain many costly, well-behaved clones for weeks before gaining influence, while honest agents earn their standing once.
